sections.title: Where Eight Centuries of Scholarship Meet Your Ambition
sections.lead: Study at Italy’s distinguished universities, from the world’s oldest seat of learning in Bologna to the design and engineering vanguard of Milan, with EUROPA FUSION guiding every step.

sections.title: An Education Rooted in History, Shaped for the Future
sections.intro: Italy is the birthplace of the university itself. Its oldest institutions have shaped law, medicine, science and the arts for a millennium, matched today by world-class modern research and low living costs.

items.title: Internationally recognised qualifications
items.desc: Degrees are recognised across Europe and globally under the Bologna Process, supporting mobility for further study and careers.

items.title: Distinctive academic strengths
items.desc: Italy is a global reference point for architecture, design, fashion, mechanical engineering, economics, physics and the humanities.

items.title: Exceptional value & regional grants
items.desc: Tuition at public universities is calculated according to family income, with regional DSU scholarships offering full fee waivers and living grants.

items.title: A setting like no other
items.desc: From the Renaissance cities of Florence, Bologna and Padua to the metropolitan energy of Milan and Rome, every campus offers a rich heritage.

sections.title: Distinguished Institutions in Italy
sections.intro: The following institutions represent key destinations available to EUROPA FUSION students.

items.name: University of Bologna
items.desc: Widely regarded as the oldest university in the world. Distinguished in law, humanities, engineering and the sciences.

items.name: University of Padua
items.desc: The historic institution where Galileo once held a chair. Renowned for medicine, physics, psychology and engineering.

items.name: Sapienza University of Rome
items.desc: One of Europe’s largest research universities, with an exceptionally broad range of disciplines and global ranking.

items.name: University of Pisa
items.desc: A long tradition of excellence in computer science, engineering, mathematics, physics and natural sciences.

items.name: Politecnico di Milano
items.desc: Italy’s leading technical university, internationally ranked top 20 globally for engineering, architecture and design.

items.name: Ca’ Foscari University of Venice
items.desc: Established as a school of commerce; today strong in economics, international relations, languages and environmental sciences.

items.name: Bocconi University
items.desc: A premier European private institution of international standing in economics, finance, management and business law.

items.name: University of Turin
items.desc: A comprehensive research university with strong links to automotive industry, management and medicine in Piedmont.

sections.title: From Enquiry to Enrolment
sections.intro: EUROPA FUSION offers a structured, transparent process so that each stage is handled with care and precision.

items.title: Profile evaluation
items.desc: Academic record, career goals, budget, and preferred city are reviewed to define a realistic shortlist.

items.title: Programme & university selection
items.desc: Courses are matched to your profile, with attention to language of instruction, entry tests and deadlines.

items.title: Documents & Universitaly pre-enrolment
items.desc: Transcripts, degree certificates, English proof, CV, motivation letter and passport prepared and submitted on Universitaly.

items.title: Entrance assessment
items.desc: Where required, preparation for tests such as TOLC, IMAT (medicine), GMAT or GRE.

items.title: Offer & credential recognition
items.desc: Acceptance confirmed; qualifications verified via CIMEA Statements of Comparability/Verification or Declaration of Value (DoV).

items.title: Student visa (Type D)
items.desc: Consulate appointment booking, file review, accommodation and financial evidence according to official Italian requirements.

items.title: Arrival & settling in
items.desc: Permesso di Soggiorno (residence permit) application, Codice Fiscale, bank setup and university matriculation.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.intro: Common questions about studying and settling in Italy.

items.q: Can I study in Italy entirely in English?
items.a: Yes. Italian universities offer hundreds of English-taught programmes, particularly at Master’s level and in fields such as engineering, business, economics, design and medicine (via IMAT). The language of instruction should be verified for each course.

items.q: Do I need to speak Italian?
items.a: It is not required for English-taught programmes, but basic Italian greatly enriches daily life and improves your prospects of finding part-time work and internships. Many universities provide free Italian language classes.

items.q: How much does it cost to study in Italy?
items.a: Italy is regarded as one of Europe’s most affordable destinations. Public university tuition is generally modest (€1,000–€4,000/yr) and is calculated according to family income (ISEE-Parificato). Living costs commonly range between €700 and €1,200 per month.

items.q: When are the intakes and deadlines?
items.a: The main intake begins in September or October, with a smaller intake in February or March at some universities. Application windows open early (between November and April), so preparing 9 to 12 months in advance is recommended.
Most English-taught programmes request evidence of proficiency, such as IELTS (normally 6.0–6.5) or TOEFL. A small number of universities accept a Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate.

items.q: Are scholarships available to international students?
items.a: Yes! Regional DSU scholarships (such as DSU Toscana, EDISU Piemonte, ER.GO, Disco Lazio) provide full tuition waivers plus free accommodation, meals and up to €6,000–€7,000/yr in cash stipends based on family income. Italian Government MAECI scholarships are also available.

items.q: Can I work while studying in Italy?
items.a: Holders of an Italian student residence permit are permitted to work part-time up to 20 hours per week, up to a legal maximum of 1,040 hours per year.

items.q: Can I remain in Italy after graduating?
items.a: Eligible Master’s and PhD graduates may apply for a 1-year Permesso di Soggiorno per Ricerca Lavoro (job-search permit) to find professional employment or register as a freelancer.
Typically: passport, academic transcripts, degree certificate, English certificate, CV, motivation letter, CIMEA certificate or Declaration of Value (DoV), and proof of financial means.

items.q: How does EUROPA FUSION support my application?
items.a: We assist with university selection, CIMEA recognition, Universitaly portal pre-enrolment, DSU scholarship application, Italian student visa file assembly, and housing guidance.
